coverage.reason: verifyPlaybackUrl reproduces mint's exact signed string (Number(exp) interpolates identically); boundaries: exp<=now expired, non-integer 'bad expiry', missing params rejected; length guard precedes timingSafeEqual so no throw path is reachable.
Pure module, sole dependency node:crypto; minimal export surface; secret read from env at call time (not require time), so test and prod secrets are picked up per invocation.

No dedicated unit tests for the pure verify branches; covered indirectly by the 11 e2e tests (missing/expired/same-length-tampered). GAP: 'bad expiry' and sig length-guard branches untested -> finding F1.
Header comment (problem/fix/TTL/secret) and JSDoc (caller must authZ before mint; pure verify) match the implementation; TTL 900 matches the e2e expires_in=900 assertion.

HMAC-SHA256 with constant-time compare and length guard; secret from DECENTRALFLIX_MEDIA_SECRET with dev-only default + startup warning; signature binds (passId, filmId, exp). Tamper/retarget/expiry all 403 in e2e.
15-minute presigned URL is the standard headerless-video pattern; satisfies Dino's chief decision and requirements R1/R2.

passPlaybackUrl order: auth(401) -> pass 404 -> holder 403 -> film param 400 -> film 404 -> entitlement 403 -> mint; no leak to strangers. mediaPlay: verify -> 403 fail-closed, film 404, CDN.streamFile honors Range (e2e: 206, exactly 100 bytes).

Reuses requireAuth/ownsFilm/hasEntitlement — the same predicates as the stream route, no duplicated policy. Clean boundary: server does authZ, lib does crypto. Routes registered in handleApi with the existing route table.

11 e2e tests cover both routes: success, authZ matrix (401/403/403), TTL=900, URL shape, headerless 200 with bytes, Range 206, tamper/retarget/expiry/missing-params 403. Assertions check codes, non-empty bodies, byte counts.
Handler comments (fail-closed 403, Range via streamFile, holder check reuses passDetail's) match the code; the startup warning text matches secretIsDefault() behavior.

Identity+authZ enforced at the mint boundary (authoritative). Play enforces signature only; entitlement is mint-time (revocation/refund propagation <= 15 min — inherent to the presigned pattern, Dino's pick, documented). No new injection surface: IDs via store lookups, params via URLSearchParams.

Mint 200 JSON {url, expires_at, expires_in, pass_id, film_id, legal_notice} matches the frontend client's snake_case expectation exactly; 401/403/404/400 used consistently with the rest of the API; mediaPlay 403 fail-closed, 404 when the film is gone.
Presigned-URL pattern resolves R1 (video cannot send headers); mint-side authZ equals stream-route authZ (R3: ownsFilm || hasEntitlement; a bare pass never grants a film).

Expired-URL fixture crafts HMAC with the same test secret and [passId,filmId,exp].join('.') — identical to signPlayback's template. Tampered sig uses 64 zeros (same length as a real sig), exercising timingSafeEqual's false path.

DF-MEDIA-3 section sits after the pass-buyer setup so PASSID/PB_TOKEN/FILM1/FILM2/OTHER_TOKEN exist and the buyer is entitled to FILM1 only; server started with the fixed test secret on the start line.
11 meaningful assertions; each fail branch prints the http code/url for diagnosis. GAP: no non-integer-exp case and no short-sig length-mismatch case -> finding F1.
Section header explains the why (video cannot send Authorization) and the fixture rationale (redeemed FILM1, not FILM2) — both accurate.
Tests assert the negative security matrix (401 + 4x403 paths). The expired fixture hardcodes the test secret matching the server start line — drift fails loudly. No real secrets in the file.

film.html reads dfl.pass_id in try/catch (private-mode safe), encodeURIComponent on both IDs, D.getJSON attaches the Bearer <redacted> (app.js:96), sets player.src on success, shows a status banner on failure. pass.html persists r.pass.pass_id after successful test subscribe. Legacy fallback preserved when no pass_id.
Two small hunks; shared localStorage key dfl.pass_id is consistent across the pages; no new dependencies.

STR-001 covers the auth helper (login stores token, helpers send Bearer); the HTML glue itself has no automated test — consistent with this repo's strategy for static pages (no browser harness). The server path is e2e-covered.
Inline comments state the why (video cannot send the header) and the legacy fallback condition — both accurate.
Error state is visible (status banner on mint failure); no loading indicator while minting (minor, noted). Player stays empty on mint failure — a visible failure, acceptable.
Native video + presigned URL is the required pattern (R1/R6); the legacy path is preserved for pass-less browsers.

snake_case -> camelCase mapping matches the server response exactly (url/expires_at/expires_in/pass_id/film_id); fallbacks apply only when url is present but fields are missing. resolvePlaybackSrc handles absolute passthrough and relative join correctly.
Module is self-contained (fetch only) but has no importers in apps/frontend — unwired scaffolding for the Next.js watch page. Complete and tested; wiring is a product-loop call, not a defect.

7 vitest tests mock fetch at the right boundary; assert endpoint URL, Authorization header on the mint call, typed 401/403, no-network on missing token, malformed body, and both resolvePlaybackSrc branches. GAP: the documented 404 path is untested -> finding F5.
Header + JSDoc describe the flow, 15-min expiry, and typed 401/403/404/transport errors — accurate against the implementation.
Bearer <redacted> is sent only on the mint call and never attached to the video src (asserted in the test); a missing token fails before any network I/O; no secret handling client-side.
Typed errors map to the server's status codes (401/403/404); 5xx/429 fall through to a generic PlaybackUrlError carrying the status — reasonable.

findings.challenge: Counter-evidence: mint and verify use the identical serialization, so a signature is only checked against the exact triple it was minted for; IDs are server-generated, so an attacker cannot arrange a colliding triple without the secret. No reachable violation.
findings.claim: Considered: ${passId}.${filmId}.${exp} dot-joined serialization could let a signature for one (pass,film) triple validate as a different triple.

findings.challenge: Counter-evidence: failure is visible (status banner), success populates the player, and the mint is a single local JSON round-trip. Cosmetic with no acceptance measure here.
findings.claim: Considered: film.html shows nothing while the mint call is in flight (no loading indicator).

findings.challenge: Counter-evidence: the oracle needs a valid pass-holder session, and the pre-existing stream route has the identical property — no new exposure introduced by this change.
findings.claim: Considered: an authenticated pass holder can distinguish film non-existence (404) from non-entitlement (403) at the mint endpoint.
